title: Hebrews Chapter 3 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Hebrews chapter 3 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Hebrews Chapter 3 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Hebrews Chapter 3.

questions.question: In Hebrews 3, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Consider the Apostle and High Priest of our profession
Moses was faithful in all his house
For every house is builded by some man
Christ as a son over his own house
questions.correctAnswer: Consider the Apostle and High Priest of our profession
questions.explanation: This appears first in the chapter as it is the opening statement in Hebrews 3:1.

questions.question: Who is referred to as the Apostle and High Priest of our profession?
questions.explanation: This is stated directly in Hebrews 3:1.

questions.question: Who was faithful to him that appointed him?
questions.explanation: This is confirmed in Hebrews 3:2 where it mentions Christ's faithfulness.

questions.question: In what way was Christ counted worthy of more glory than Moses?
options: He is the Son of God
questions.explanation: Hebrews 3:3 explains that Christ, who built the house, has more honor than the house itself.

questions.question: According to Hebrews 3:4, who built all things?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 3:4 states that he that built all things is God.

questions.question: What role did Moses serve in his house?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 3:5 describes Moses as faithful in all his house, as a servant.

questions.question: What condition is mentioned for being part of Christ's house?
options: If we hold fast the confidence
questions.correctAnswer: If we hold fast the confidence
questions.explanation: Hebrews 3:6 states that we are part of His house if we hold fast the confidence and hope.

questions.question: What does the Holy Ghost say in Hebrews 3:7?
options: To today if you will hear his voice
questions.correctAnswer: To today if you will hear his voice
questions.explanation: This is a direct quote from Hebrews 3:7, indicating what the Holy Ghost says.

questions.question: Who was faithful in all his house?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 3:5 clearly states that Moses was faithful in all his house.

questions.question: What is the relationship of Christ to His house according to Hebrews 3:6?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 3:6 describes Christ as a son over His own house.

questions.question: Christ is considered more glorious than Moses because He has what?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 3:3 indicates that Christ has more glory than Moses.

questions.question: True or False: The Holy Ghost speaks in Hebrews 3:7.
questions.explanation: Hebrews 3:7 states that the Holy Ghost saith, confirming that it speaks.

questions.question: True or False: Moses was a servant in his own house.
questions.explanation: Hebrews 3:5 states that Moses was faithful as a servant in his house.

questions.question: True or False: Christ built everything except the house.
questions.explanation: Hebrews 3:4 states that God built all things, not excluding the house.

questions.question: True or False: Moses is considered the Apostle and High Priest of our profession.
questions.explanation: Hebrews 3:1 identifies Christ Jesus as the Apostle and High Priest, not Moses.

medium.title: Hebrews Chapter 3 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Hebrews Chapter 3 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What should we not do, as stated in Hebrews 3:8?
questions.explanation: The verse clearly states, 'Harden not your hearts, as in the provocation...'

questions.question: What does Hebrews 3:12 promise will happen if someone takes heed to avoid an evil heart of unbelief?
options: They will enter into God's rest
They will be partakers of Christ
questions.correctAnswer: They will be partakers of Christ
questions.explanation: Taking heed helps one to maintain a faithful heart, leading to being partakers of Christ as stated in Hebrews 3:14.

questions.question: What was God's reaction to the generation mentioned in Hebrews 3:10?
questions.explanation: The verse indicates that God was 'grieved with that generation' due to their continual errors.

questions.question: What does Hebrews 3:11 indicate about those who err in their hearts?
options: They shall not enter into My rest
questions.correctAnswer: They shall not enter into My rest
questions.explanation: This is the consequence stated in the verse for those who err in their hearts.

questions.question: According to Hebrews 3:13, what should we do daily?
questions.explanation: The verse explicitly instructs that we should 'exhort one another daily'.

questions.question: What is the result of being hardened through the deceitfulness of sin, as mentioned in Hebrews 3:13?
questions.explanation: The context shows that hardening hearts leads to a departure from God.

questions.question: What does Hebrews 3:14 say we must do to be made partakers of Christ?
options: Hold the beginning of our confidence steadfast
questions.correctAnswer: Hold the beginning of our confidence steadfast
questions.explanation: The verse states that we are made partakers of Christ if we 'hold the beginning of our confidence stedfast unto the end'.

questions.question: In Hebrews 3:1, who are referred to as 'holy brethren'?
questions.explanation: The verse addresses 'holy brethren, partakers of the heavenly calling'.

questions.question: What is stated about Jesus in Hebrews 3:2?
questions.explanation: The verse confirms that Jesus was 'faithful to him that appointed him'.

questions.question: According to Hebrews 3:6, what are we if we hold fast the confidence and the rejoicing of the hope?
questions.explanation: The verse states that 'whose house are we' if we hold firm our confidence.

questions.question: What does Hebrews 3:7 encourage us to do today?
questions.explanation: The verse urges us to 'consider the Apostle and High Priest of our profession, Christ Jesus'.

questions.question: What is the main warning of Hebrews 3:12?
options: To not have an evil heart of unbelief
questions.correctAnswer: To not have an evil heart of unbelief
questions.explanation: The verse explicitly warns against having an 'evil heart of unbelief'.

questions.question: True or False: According to Hebrews 3:11, those who err in their hearts shall enter into rest.
questions.explanation: Hebrews 3:11 states, 'They shall not enter into my rest', indicating that erring hearts cannot enter.

questions.question: True or False: Hebrews 3:13 encourages us to exhort one another daily.
questions.explanation: The verse positively commands us to 'exhort one another daily'.

questions.question: True or False: Hebrews 3:8 instructs us to harden our hearts in times of temptation.
questions.explanation: The verse instructs the opposite: 'Harden not your hearts'.

hard.title: Hebrews Chapter 3 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Hebrews Chapter 3.

questions.question: What does Hebrews 3:15 urge the audience not to do?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 3:15 states, 'harden not your hearts, as in the provocation,' urging readers to be receptive to God's voice.

questions.question: According to Hebrews 3:16, who provoked God?
options: All that came out of Egypt
questions.explanation: Hebrews 3:16 specifies that 'some, when they had heard, did provoke,' indicating that not all were disobedient.

questions.question: In Hebrews 3:17, with whom was God grieved for forty years?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 3:17 asks, 'was it not with them that had sinned, whose carcases fell in the wilderness?' referring to the Israelites.

questions.question: Who did God swear would not enter His rest according to Hebrews 3:18?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 3:18 states, 'to whom sware he that they should not enter into his rest, but to them that believed not?'

questions.question: What is the reason given in Hebrews 3:19 for why they could not enter in?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 3:19 concludes that 'they could not enter in because of unbelief,' emphasizing the critical nature of faith.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'parakaleō' in Hebrews 3:13 mean?
questions.explanation: 'Parakaleō' is used in Hebrews 3:13, meaning 'to exhort or encourage,' indicating the need for mutual support in faith.

questions.question: Which literary technique is used in Hebrews 3:7-8?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 3:7-8 demonstrates parallelism by repeating the call to heed God's voice and the warning against hardening hearts.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to the theme of unbelief as seen in Hebrews 3:19?
questions.explanation: Matthew 13:58 states, 'And he did not do many mighty works there because of their unbelief,' paralleling the theme of disbelief in Hebrews 3:19.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage fulfills the concept of God's rest mentioned in Hebrews 3:18?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 4:9 speaks of 'a rest for the people of God,' fulfilling the promise found in Hebrews 3:18 about entering rest.

questions.question: What comes before Hebrews 3:15?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 3:14 precedes Hebrews 3:15, stating that 'For we are made partakers of Christ, if we hold the beginning of our confidence stedfast unto the end.'

questions.question: What follows Hebrews 3:18?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 3:19 directly follows Hebrews 3:18, explaining that 'they could not enter in because of unbelief.'

questions.question: The warning against an evil heart of unbelief in Hebrews 3:12 reflects a theme found in which Old Testament passage?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 4:23 advises, 'Keep thy heart with all diligence; for out of it are the issues of life,' echoing the warning in Hebrews 3:12.

questions.question: The exhortation to encourage one another in Hebrews 3:13 is crucial for what reason?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 3:13 states, 'lest any of you be hardened through the deceitfulness of sin,' emphasizing the importance of mutual exhortation.

questions.question: True or False: Hebrews 3:11 expresses God's promise that all will enter His rest.
questions.explanation: Hebrews 3:11 states, 'So I sware in my wrath, They shall not enter into my rest,' indicating that not all will enter.

questions.question: True or False: In Hebrews 3:10, God was grieved with a generation for their faithfulness.
questions.explanation: Hebrews 3:10 states, 'Wherefore I was grieved with that generation,' referring to their error and unfaithfulness.

theological.title: Hebrews Chapter 3 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Hebrews Chapter 3 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Hebrews 3:6 teach about the nature of salvation and the believer's relationship to Christ?
options: Christ is a son over His own house, and believers are His house if they hold fast their confidence and hope
Believers are servants in the house of God under Moses's authority
Salvation is obtained through adherence to the law given by Moses
Christ is a high priest who mediates a temporary covenant for the house of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: Christ is a son over His own house, and believers are His house if they hold fast their confidence and hope
questions.explanation: Hebrews 3:6 states that Christ is a son over His own house, and we are His house if we hold fast the confidence and hope to the end, teaching the doctrine of believers' union with Christ and perseverance in salvation.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning human sin and unbelief does Hebrews 3:12 teach?
options: Believers must beware of an evil heart of unbelief that causes departure from the living God
Sin is only external and does not affect the heart
Unbelief is a minor issue that does not separate one from God
Departing from God can be corrected by merely verbal confession
questions.correctAnswer: Believers must beware of an evil heart of unbelief that causes departure from the living God
questions.explanation: Hebrews 3:12 warns believers to take heed lest any have an evil heart of unbelief, which leads to departing from the living God, highlighting the seriousness of unbelief as sin.

questions.question: What doctrine about Christ's superiority over Moses is taught in Hebrews 3:3?
options: Christ is worthy of more glory than Moses because the builder of the house has more honor than the house
Moses and Christ share equal glory as leaders of God's people
Christ is a servant like Moses but with different responsibilities
Moses was glorified because he built the house of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: Christ is worthy of more glory than Moses because the builder of the house has more honor than the house
questions.explanation: Hebrews 3:3 explains Christ's superiority over Moses by stating that the builder of the house has more honor than the house, affirming Christ's divine status.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Hebrews 3:4 specifically demonstrate?
options: God's sovereignty as the builder of all things
questions.correctAnswer: God's sovereignty as the builder of all things
questions.explanation: Hebrews 3:4 states that every house is built by someone, but God is the builder of all things, demonstrating His sovereignty over creation.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is illustrated in Hebrews 3:10 when God is grieved by Israel's continual error and disobedience?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 3:10 shows God's grief and wrath against a generation that errs continually, reflecting His holiness and righteous anger against sin.

questions.question: How does Hebrews 3 prepare the reader for the theme of entering God's rest found in later chapters and Psalms?
options: By warning against unbelief and disobedience that prevent entering God's rest
By emphasizing works-based righteousness as the path to rest
By focusing solely on Moses' leadership and not Christ's
By teaching that rest is only a physical cessation from labor
questions.correctAnswer: By warning against unbelief and disobedience that prevent entering God's rest
questions.explanation: Hebrews 3:7-19 connects Israel's wilderness unbelief with missing God's rest, preparing for later exhortations (Hebrews 4) regarding the spiritual rest available through faith.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical connection does Hebrews 3:5-6 make between Moses and Christ?
options: Moses was faithful as a servant, but Christ as a son over God's house, showing progression in revelation
Both Moses and Christ were servants with equal authority
Christ is just another prophet like Moses with no superiority
Moses' role is irrelevant compared to Christ
questions.correctAnswer: Moses was faithful as a servant, but Christ as a son over God's house, showing progression in revelation
questions.explanation: Hebrews 3:5-6 contrasts Moses' faithfulness as a servant with Christ's position as son over God's house, highlighting the fulfillment and superiority of Christ in redemptive history.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Hebrews 3:12 and Hebrews 3:14 teach about perseverance and faith?
options: Unbelief leads to departure from God, but holding confidence steadfast ensures participation in Christ
Faith is irrelevant to perseverance in the Christian life
Unbelief is a minor flaw easily overcome without perseverance
Perseverance depends solely on human effort without divine aid
questions.correctAnswer: Unbelief leads to departure from God, but holding confidence steadfast ensures participation in Christ
questions.explanation: Hebrews 3:12 warns against an evil heart of unbelief causing departure from God, while 3:14 affirms that holding our original confidence steadfast makes us partakers of Christ, showing the necessity of persevering faith.

questions.question: What combined teaching do Hebrews 3:7-8 and Hebrews 3:15 give about God's warning to His people?
options: God warns His people not to harden their hearts as in the wilderness provocation
God encourages His people to harden their hearts against temptation
God's warnings are optional and not urgent
God's voice is only for the Old Testament generation
questions.correctAnswer: God warns His people not to harden their hearts as in the wilderness provocation
questions.explanation: Both Hebrews 3:7-8 and 3:15 cite the warning to not harden hearts as in the wilderness, emphasizing the ongoing relevance of God's call to obedience and faithfulness.

questions.question: What synthesis of doctrine about unbelief and God's rest is taught in Hebrews 3:18-19 and Hebrews 3:11?
options: Those who disbelieve will not enter God's rest, as God swore in wrath
Unbelief has no effect on entering God's rest
God's rest is guaranteed regardless of belief
God's wrath is unrelated to unbelief
questions.correctAnswer: Those who disbelieve will not enter God's rest, as God swore in wrath
questions.explanation: Hebrews 3:11 records God's oath that the disobedient generation would not enter rest, and 3:18-19 reiterate unbelief as the cause of exclusion from God's rest.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Hebrews 3:16-19 teaches that God's judgment was unjust because the entire generation was punished. What does the text actually teach?
options: Judgment was on those who sinned and disbelieved, not all who came out of Egypt
The punishment was random and unfair
The text teaches universal salvation despite sin
questions.correctAnswer: Judgment was on those who sinned and disbelieved, not all who came out of Egypt
questions.explanation: Hebrews 3:16-19 clarifies that God was grieved with those who sinned and disbelieved, whose bodies fell in the wilderness, not all who came out under Moses.

questions.question: What doctrine about Christ's faithfulness is taught in Hebrews 3:2?
options: Christ was faithful to God who appointed Him, paralleling Moses' faithfulness
Christ was unfaithful but redeemed later
Moses was faithful but Christ was not
Faithfulness is irrelevant to Christ's work
questions.correctAnswer: Christ was faithful to God who appointed Him, paralleling Moses' faithfulness
questions.explanation: Hebrews 3:2 states that Christ was faithful to Him who appointed Him, just as Moses was faithful in all his house, affirming Christ's perfect obedience.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is revealed in Hebrews 3:9 regarding God's interaction with Israel during their wilderness journey?
options: God's longsuffering in bearing with Israel for forty years
questions.correctAnswer: God's longsuffering in bearing with Israel for forty years
questions.explanation: Hebrews 3:9 records that God was tested and grieved by Israel's rebellion over forty years, showing His longsuffering patience.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical insight does Hebrews 3:1 provide about Christ's identity in relation to the new covenant?
options: Christ is the Apostle and High Priest of our profession, indicating His unique mediatorial role
Christ is a mere prophet like Moses
Christ has no role in the new covenant
Christ is only a political leader
questions.correctAnswer: Christ is the Apostle and High Priest of our profession, indicating His unique mediatorial role
questions.explanation: Hebrews 3:1 calls Christ the Apostle and High Priest of our profession, affirming His dual role as messenger and mediator in the new covenant.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Hebrews 3:13 and Hebrews 3:15 teach about the community's role in sanctification and the danger of sin?
options: Believers must exhort one another daily to prevent hardening hearts through sin's deceitfulness
Sanctification is a solitary process without community involvement
Sin does not affect the community's spiritual health
Exhortation is unnecessary because sin is obvious
questions.correctAnswer: Believers must exhort one another daily to prevent hardening hearts through sin's deceitfulness
questions.explanation: Hebrews 3:13 urges daily mutual exhortation to avoid being hardened by sin, echoed in 3:15's warning not to harden hearts, emphasizing community responsibility in sanctification.
